But I just wanted to add one more sentence. You have noticed that there is a certain degree of dissatisfaction in this courtroom. Your Honour Judge Antonetti has referred to it a couple of days ago. Much of it can be attributed to the length and fatigue, but these are details that affect the condition of the accused. These are a million details which contribute to the whole picture. And things like this have an impact too, and we must bear this in mind. And if necessary, we will seek the assistance of the Chamber regarding further steps regarding this and similar documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to bring the witness in for re-examination. Mr. Karnavas, a question of a technical nature. Your client authorised you to represent him, did he not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, I wasn't -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat my question. Did Mr. Prlic authorise you to continue to represent him because the witness is coming back?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, he has. And as I've indicated he was waived his presence. He is not withdrawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my understanding. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, we apologise for keeping you waiting a little longer than planned because the pause was longer than we envisaged because we had some procedural matters to deal with. Madam Nozica will a have some additional questions for you, and I give her the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I will have an additional question with regard to a single document, very briefly. It was used in the examination-in-chief. I haven't prepared it, and I apologise for this. It is in my binder for the examination-in-chief. We are all very well familiar with it. It is the third from the back.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Buljan, you don't have to look for it. You will see it in the e-court. I would like to call document P 04756. Mr. Buljan, you were asked several times by my learned friend whether welfare was provided to members of the Muslim nation after the events, and I repeat, after the events of the 9th of May, and the 30th of June, 1993. I should like to ask you to take a look at this document which you have seen during the proofing. This is a document dated the 2nd of September, 1993 after -- which means after both these two events in Mostar. Let us look at page 5 of the Croatian version which is page 7 of the English version. So I'm referring to the part that I showed you in the direct examination. The new structure has been adopted and the conclusion was adopted that families of killed members of the HVO of Muslim ethnicity continued to be provided benefits. Mr. Buljan, is this report from the collegium of the Defence Department an information that you had and that corroborates what you said that Muslim members of the HVO were cared for even after the events of the 9th of May and the 30th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: STIPO BULJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question. I can confirm with full responsibility that the organisation of welfare applied to all members of the HVO regardless of their ethnicity up to this date and after this date.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Buljan. I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours. That brings to an end my re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Buljan, on behalf of my colleagues, I wish to thank you for coming at the request of one of the parties to testify. I wish you all the best upon your return to your country and success in your future work. I'm going to ask the usher to be kind enough to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica, for next week we have two witnesses who have been planned. Unless I'm mistaken, you said that these witnesses will come, the distribution of time has already been indicated. On the Prosecution side there are no problems regarding the summaries. You are not going to come and tell us at the last minute that the summaries will not allow you to do the cross-examination, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we -- the Prosecution has been in contact with the Stojic Defence about the summaries that we identified that we believe need to be improved. We've done it informally by letter, and I have the expectation that this matter will be resolved without the need to resort to rulings of the Trial Chamber. The witness for next week is one of the witnesses, and I believe that sufficient information has come in and that there are not going to be any witness summary issues related to that witness. It was my understanding that we only had one witness for next week and not two, if I could add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. My learned friend is quite right, I wish to say that Mr. Stojic's Defence will do its best to cooperate with our colleagues from the Prosecution. All the requests coming from them, which we consider to be well-founded, will meet with our understanding. Your Honour we have one witness for next week, Veso Vegar, who will be examined for three hours, and as far as I understood you, we will not have a break on Wednesday. We will be working on Wednesday and not on Thursday. So this witness can stay in the courtroom for three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except if we need to continue on Thursday, we will continue on Thursday. If we finish on Wednesday, we finish, but one never knows; it may be necessary to continue on Thursday, but for the moment Thursday is free. So there will be no problems, I hope. In that case I'm going to adjourn. I wish you all a good day and we meet again next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of February, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.47 p.m.
